title: Layered config resolution with one effective-value view (defaults ⊕ user ⊕ operator overlay)
contract: `load_config()` builds the effective dict once: deepcopy(DEFAULT_CONFIG) → deep-merge the user's config.yaml (a user `None` cannot wipe a dict section) → normalise model/max_turns aliases → `${VAR}` expand → deep-merge the managed overlay on top, cached on a `(user_mtime, size, managed_mtime, size)` signature plus a snapshot of every referenced env var so a late `.env` load re-expands (22-config-b.md `config-b.core.load_config`, hermes_cli/config.py:3936-4092). Every reader in the product imports the same function, so `hermes config get` and the dashboard show the same value the agent sees.

title: Operator-pinned settings a user cannot change (managed scope)
contract: `/etc/hermes/config.yaml` + `/etc/hermes/.env` (or `$HERMES_MANAGED_DIR`) are deep-merged ON TOP of the user's config leaf by leaf, so IT pins individual keys without freezing the rest. Every writer is gated: `config set`/`unset` exit 1 with 'managed by your administrator', `save_config` strips managed leaves from bulk writes and reports which, `save_env_value` refuses. Managed `${VAR}` refs expand only against the process env so a user ref cannot shadow a pinned literal (22-config-b.md `config-b.core.managed_scope`, managed_scope.py:56-176).
governance: privileged — the pin file is the policy source, so pin reads stay read-only, but any writer that discovers a pinned key must refuse before the kernel is consulted; the refusal belongs in the same path as the `config.write` kind proposed below

title: Surviving a corrupt or unreadable config store without silently losing policy
contract: A YAML parse failure warns once per `(path, mtime, size)`, snapshots the file to `config.yaml.corrupt.<ts>.bak`, and then either keeps the last successfully loaded config for a running process or falls back to defaults for a fresh one — a port of openai/codex#31188 whose stated motivation is not dropping security-critical overrides such as `approvals.deny`. `require_readable_config_before_write()` makes every writer refuse rather than overwrite an unparseable file (22-config-b.md `config-b.core.corrupt_config_recovery`, config.py:48-165, 3612-3696).
governance: read-only, but this is the row that protects every privileged setting — a load failure that silently restores permissive defaults is a policy downgrade with no audit record

title: Command-line access to configuration on a box with no working server
contract: `hermes config show|edit|get|set|unset|path|env-path|check|migrate`. `get`/`set`/`unset` take dotted key paths with `\.` escaping, greedy literal matching for keys that contain dots (model ids, Matrix room ids), and a phantom-sibling refusal that stops a set from shadowing an existing dotted key; `set` coerces to the type of the default, refuses to overwrite a mapping section with a scalar unless `--force`, masks credential-shaped leaves in its echo, and prints a difflib 'did you mean' on an unknown key. `path`/`env-path` print the resolved files; `check` prints the schema version and which optional env vars are set (22-config-b.md §A2, config.py:5559-6255).
governance: privileged — a CLI write must go through the same `config.write` mediation as the HTTP route, or it becomes the documented way to bypass the kernel

title: Config schema versioning and a migration ladder
contract: `_config_version: 39` in the file, a support floor at 12 ('this config predates version 12 and can no longer be auto-migrated'), and a registry of `(target_version, fn)` steps gated on the on-disk version — renames (`write_mode`→`write_approval`), re-shapes (flat `stt.model`→provider section, `custom_providers` list→`providers` dict), retirements (drop the `bfl` toolset from saved lists, remove retired plugin keys), and value corrections that only fire if the old default is untouched. Post-migration it disables MCP servers that fail validation and prompts for env vars and skill settings introduced since the old version; `_persist_migration` never materialises pure defaults (22-config-b.md `config-b.core.migrations`, config_migrations.py:53-910).

title: Config-driven data lifecycle — prune, archive, vacuum on an interval-gated sweep
contract: 13 `sessions.*` keys plus a parallel `checkpoints.*` block: `auto_prune`/`retention_days` (90) deletes ended sessions by last activity, `auto_archive`/`auto_archive_days` (3) soft-hides them and exempts pinned ones, `vacuum_after_prune`/`min_vacuum_interval_days` (30) runs SQLite VACUUM only when a prune actually deleted rows, and `min_interval_hours` (24) gates the whole sweep through a `state_meta` row shared across processes. Motivated by 384MB databases with 68K messages (22-config-b.md §T, gateway/run.py:7745-7790).
governance: privileged and irreversible — a retention TTL change schedules deletion of owner data, so the setting write is exactly the case for the irreversible tier; the sweep itself is internal maintenance
